answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. If several identities controlled by one attacker collude, cryptographic links between their deposits let the system slash the full stake when they violate a shared rule, rather than treating each account as independent. Splitting one identity into many therefore multiplies the capital at risk; walnut, onyx, and sable can be harmless account names, but they do not make the deposits free.
